question: can the centre keep its special role -- the clock-hand hinge whose cost does not care where the mouths are -- without being a point?
answer: yes, and the hinge is cheaper than the proposal assumed: the geodesic turn cost is quadratic, T(alpha) = alpha^2/(2I), not the bearing's arc f0*alpha
turn_cost_law: T(alpha) = alpha^2 / (2I) = alpha^2 * conductance / (8 pi);  I -> 4/f0 gives f0 alpha^2/8

checks.name: the arms are the repo's geometry, symmetry dropped
*** the arms are independent INTRINSICALLY (attachment caveat) ***

detail.why_it_matters: the old vacuole picture had to give the inner and outer boundaries one shared arbitrary radial gap; a finite bearing with two arms has no such constraint
detail.what_loses_significance: the vacuole's ARBITRARY DRAWING ratio, which was never identified with the endpoint scales -- NOT the endpoint scale ratio itself, which is load-bearing: w_i/w_o = f_i/f_o

matched_mouths_would_be_equal.why: C1 matching to a unit round S^3 forces f0 = sin^3 a_j = F_j^3 at each end, so one common f0 fixes F = f0^(1/3) uniquely

detail.this_is_an_intrinsic_statement_not_a_mat: unequal arms are honest truncations of one scalar-flat profile; they are NOT a fully matched #265 throat with the symmetry removed, because that matching forces F_o = F_i

detail.what_is_transported: the ANGULAR width, which is constant along the route; the physical width is not
detail.why_not_bitwise: the drawn ratio is (f_i dtheta)/(f_o dtheta), and the two products round separately -- the identity is exact, the two multiplications are not

checks.name: *** the turn cost is quadratic, not linear ***

detail.law: T(alpha) = alpha^2/(2 I2) + O(alpha^4),  I2 = int ds/f^2
detail.the_law_is_leading_order: the exact object is the Clairaut-integrated turn_cost; the quadratic is its leading term, and the next one is -alpha^4 I4/(8 I2^4)
detail.conductance_form: T(alpha) = alpha^2 * conductance / (8 pi) + O(alpha^4), at angular dimension q = 2
detail.what_was_proposed: L_turn ~ f0 alpha, the bearing's arc length
detail.what_is_measured: T(alpha) = alpha^2/(2 I2) + O(alpha^4), quadratic in the angle and much smaller -- the geodesic spreads the turn instead of paying it as pure transverse motion, so the cost is second order rather than first

checks.name: the linear guess is an upper bound, and loose

detail.why: the geodesic starts turning while it is still descending, where f is larger and a given angle costs less arc

checks.name: *** the hinge is never the expensive part ***

detail.pi_is_the_largest_separation: bearing_distance reduces any pair of directions to [0, pi], so the alpha = pi row is the worst case over the whole configuration space
detail.the_break_even_angle_is_withdrawn: sqrt(2 I2 L) lands past pi, but it extrapolates the small-angle quadratic law outside its domain AND outside the bearing's configuration space, so it is not a physical angle; only the fact that it exceeds pi carries any content
detail.what_this_does_not_say: that the cost is zero -- it is finite, and linear in f0, which is exactly the difference between a bearing and a point

checks.name: the point model is the limit, not a rival

detail.limit: L_o + L_i, independent of where the mouths are

checks.name: *** intersection becomes overlap on the bearing ***

detail.criterion: they meet iff the angular extents overlap: |separation| < (w_a + w_b)/2
detail.whether_is_an_angular_question: f0 does not appear in the criterion
detail.how_big_depends_on_the_bearing_dimension: on the drawn S^1 cross-section the overlap is a LENGTH, f0 x (overlap angle); on an S^2 bearing an AREA ~ f0^2 x (angular area); on S^3 a VOLUME ~ f0^3 x (angular volume). The yes/no criterion is dimension-free; the size law is not
detail.the_point_limit_correctly_stated: as f0 -> 0 the ANGULAR INCIDENCE SURVIVES and the PHYSICAL INTERACTION REGION COLLAPSES: which directions the fronts come in at, and whether their extents overlap, are untouched by f0; the region in which they actually share space is f0 x (overlap angle) and goes to zero. So f0 -> 0 does NOT make every route meet -- it shrinks the overlap AND the gap together, and the distinction survives as a yes/no while disappearing as a length
detail.what_survives_the_limit: angular incidence -- direction of arrival and angular overlap, neither of which involves f0
detail.what_collapses: the physical interaction region, f0 x (overlap angle), and equally the physical separation of fronts that miss

checks.name: the drawn circle is honest; the identification bites

detail.why_dimension_free: two directions span a totally geodesic 2-plane, so the walk is a great-circle arc on S^1, S^2 or S^3 alike

checks.name: the law is about necks; the large-angle deficit is not

detail.why_the_law_is_general: minimising int f^2 theta'^2/2 ds at fixed int theta' ds = alpha gives theta' = h/f^2, so alpha = h I and the excess is h^2 I/2 = alpha^2/(2I) -- the profile enters only through I
detail.so_what_is_general: the quadratic law T = alpha^2/(2I) is a statement about necks; the ~8-11% deficit at a half turn is a statement about a particular one

checks.name: *** the leading form is universal; I4 is the first extra moment ***

detail.eight_digits_is_a_different_quantity: how well EACH profile matches its OWN quartic law (7.9e-09 at alpha = 0.1), not how well the two match each other (4.3e-05)
detail.i4_is_not_the_entire_profile_dependence: I6 and beyond enter at O(alpha^6); at alpha = pi the quartic prediction misses by 7.2e-03
detail.expansion: T = alpha^2/(2 I2) - alpha^4 I4/(8 I2^4) + O(alpha^6)

hyperbolic.closed_form: I2 = pi/f0, I4 = pi/(2 f0^3), shape = 1 - alpha^2/(8 pi^2)

detail.the_division_of_labour: the LEADING FUNCTIONAL FORM alpha^2/(2 I2) is universal -- every neck obeys it with its own I2, which is NOT itself universal (4/f0 here, pi/f0 there); at q = 2 that I2 is also the monopole resistance; I4 is the first ADDITIONAL INDEPENDENT MOMENT to enter, and the first place the neck's shape is felt

checks.name: *** one Dirichlet form -- and it is a q = 2 statement ***

detail.form: E[phi] = int w phi'^2 ds, minimised at fixed increment
detail.euler_lagrange: (w phi')' = 0, so w phi' is conserved
detail.the_weights_are_not_automatically_the_sa: the azimuth's weight is the METRIC coefficient f^2 for every bearing dimension; the monopole's is the VOLUME element f^q for an S^q cross-section, so its resistance is int ds/f^q
detail.and_q_equals_two_is_the_physical_case: a three-dimensional spatial throat with S^2 cross-sections, which is what physical_throat carries -- so the identity holds where it is used, but it is not dimension-free, unlike the great-circle reduction of the hinge itself
detail.as_a_potential: phi = u: the current is the flux 4 pi f^2 u', the drop is Phi I2 / 4 pi, the conductance is 4 pi / I2
detail.as_an_azimuth: phi = theta: the current is Clairaut's h = f^2 theta', the sweep is h I2, the cost is h^2 I2 / 2
detail.why_it_is_not_a_coincidence: the weight in the Dirichlet form is the transverse area element f^2, and both the monopole potential and the azimuth are functions on the tube with no angular dependence -- so they solve the same equation with the same measure, and I2 is the resistance to either
detail.what_is_not_claimed: that the two remain the same beyond leading order -- at finite alpha the geodesic picks up I4 and the static potential does not

checks.name: *** the turn sits AT the neck -- a corrected explanation ***

detail.clairaut: theta' = h/f^2, so the angular RATE is highest where f is SMALLEST
detail.the_corrected_reason: Pythagoras, not leverage: the corner pays the angle as PURE transverse motion (f0 alpha, first order) while the geodesic TILTS motion that is already radial (half f^2 theta'^2 ds, second order)
detail.what_the_first_draft_said: that the geodesic turns where the lever arm f is longer and a given angle costs less arc -- backwards on both counts
